list: The official 55 trophies, as listed 2026-11-18 (Exophase and PSNProfiles, agreeing on every name, description and grade). Guides are this entry's own words.
platinum_note: About 200 hours, difficulty 4/10, one playthrough, no online trophies, no mission replay — keep a manual save at the start of every chapter. Sources: PowerPyx GTA 6 trophy guide; KeenGamer GTA 6 trophy guide.

trophies.guide: The platinum pops automatically the moment you earn the other 54 trophies, so there is no separate task to chase here. Treat it as the finish line of the whole roadmap below: story first, then the 100% completion checklist, then the long grinds like 250 stunts and 42 shooting-range gold medals, and finally the miscellaneous cleanup. Early community estimates put the full journey at around 200 hours at a relaxed pace, with no online trophies and no difficulty setting to worry about, so the only real enemy is the sheer amount of content. Keep a manual save at the start of every chapter, because the game has no mission replay, and do the one potentially missable meditation in Chapter 1 before you move on.
trophies.name: Vice Got a Price!
sources: Official trophy list via Exophase and PSNProfiles
PowerPyx — GTA 6 trophy guide and roadmap (platinum time and difficulty)

trophies.guide: This is the very first story trophy and it unlocks naturally when you finish the opening mission, Gone Fishing, at the start of Chapter 1. You cannot miss it: just play through the mission's beats — follow the on-screen prompts, drive where the game points you, and finish the scene. It is the game's way of welcoming you to Leonida, and it pops the moment the mission's end card appears. If you are trophy hunting from minute one, use this mission to get comfortable with driving, the weapon wheel and the new switching between Jason and Lucia, because every later mission builds on exactly these controls.
trophies.name: Just Like Paradise
sources: Official trophy list via Exophase and PSNProfiles
PowerPyx — GTA 6 trophy guide (story trophies unlock naturally)

trophies.guide: Finish every main mission in Chapter 1 and this trophy unlocks when the chapter closes. Before you leave Chapter 1, do the one thing in the whole game that early guides flag as potentially missable: after the mission Down to Earth, talk to Lucia in the kitchen in the morning and accept her invitation to meditate on the balcony at Jason's house. That first meditation may count toward Positive Mental Attitude, and the opportunity disappears once the chapter ends. Also make a manual save at the start of the chapter and another right before it ends, since there is no mission replay to fall back on. Everything else in Chapter 1 can be revisited later in free roam.
trophies.name: Paradise Lost
sources: Official trophy list via Exophase and PSNProfiles
PowerPyx — GTA 6 trophy guide (Chapter 1 meditation warning)
KeenGamer — GTA 6 trophy guide (missable meditation)

trophies.guide: Play through Chapter 2's main missions to the end and the trophy unlocks as the chapter closes. Chapter 2 is where the map really opens up: both Jason and Lucia become playable together, which is when most side activities, strangers, collectibles and the wider Leonida map become available, so resist the urge to rush straight through the story. Use the chapter to scan unfamiliar vehicles with the WAiNK app and study animals through binoculars as you travel, since the 100% checklist later asks for 200 of 277 vehicles and 100 of 255 animals. Keep a manual save at the chapter's start, and enjoy the side content that unlocks here — it all counts toward the long grind later.
trophies.name: T**s Ass Drug Money
sources: Official trophy list via Exophase and PSNProfiles
PowerPyx — GTA 6 trophy guide (Chapter 2 opens the map)
KeenGamer — GTA 6 trophy guide (scan vehicles and animals as you go)

trophies.guide: Complete all of Chapter 3's main missions and this trophy pops when the chapter ends. By now the story is in full swing and new mission givers and activities keep appearing across Vice City and the rest of Leonida, so keep an eye on the map for optional missions marked with hourglass icons — some of those expire when the chapter advances, and while they do not block any trophy, they are the easiest way to meet new characters and open their mission strands. Keep rotating your manual saves, one per chapter, so you always have a fallback. If you have been scanning vehicles and studying animals as you travel, your 100% checklist will already be well on its way by the time this chapter closes.
trophies.name: Vice City, Baby!
sources: Official trophy list via Exophase and PSNProfiles
PowerPyx — GTA 6 trophy guide (optional missions expire per chapter)

trophies.guide: Finish Chapter 4's main missions and the trophy unlocks at the chapter's close, leaving only the final stretch of the story ahead. This is a good moment to take stock before the finale: check your progress screen, see how many of the 80 Challenges you have finished, and mop up any side strands or activities you have been putting off, because the endgame is a better time for cleanup than for discovering whole new systems. Keep a fresh manual save at the start of this chapter and another before the final mission, since there is no mission replay and the ending branches on choices you make. The story trophies themselves cannot be missed — they unlock as you play — so just enjoy the chapter.
trophies.name: Top Of The World, Ma
sources: Official trophy list via Exophase and PSNProfiles
PowerPyx — GTA 6 trophy guide (no mission replay; keep manual saves)

trophies.guide: Finish the game's final mission and this gold trophy unlocks with the credits. It is the only gold trophy tied directly to the story, and it cannot be missed — just play the finale to its conclusion. Before you start it, make a manual save: early guides note that the ending branches on choices and on the state of Jason and Lucia's relationship, and with no mission replay a save is your only way back if you want to see another outcome or check a choice-related trophy. Once the credits roll, free roam continues across all of Leonida, so nothing you still need for the platinum is locked away — the long cleanup phase for 100% completion starts here.
trophies.name: You Gotta Know When to Get Off
sources: Official trophy list via Exophase and PSNProfiles
PowerPyx — GTA 6 trophy guide (free roam after the story; no mission replay)
KeenGamer — GTA 6 trophy guide (final mission, relationship endings)

trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Breakfast Run and the trophy unlocks when it ends. Like every named story mission trophy, this one is unmissable: it pops automatically as you play through the campaign, with no extra objective to complete and no special condition to meet. Just follow the mission's objectives, watch the prompts, and finish the job. If you are tracking your progress, this is one of the early mission trophies that fills in during the first chapters, so it is a good early check that your checklist is working. There is nothing to prepare in advance and nothing to do differently — simply play the mission when the story offers it.
trophies.name: Trust
sources: Official trophy list via Exophase and PSNProfiles
PowerPyx — GTA 6 trophy guide (story mission trophies unlock naturally)

trophies.guide: Complete the story mission The Cartel Heist and the trophy unlocks at its conclusion. This is a story mission trophy, so it cannot be missed: play the mission when it appears in the campaign and finish it. Heist missions in GTA 6 tend to be longer, multi-stage jobs with driving, shooting and a getaway, so go in with full health and armor, a stocked weapon wheel, and a fast car parked nearby for the escape if the mission lets you plan ahead. The trophy pops the moment the mission's end screen appears, and it counts toward your story progress whether you finish it cleanly or messily — there are no mission medals in this game, so do not restart for a better grade.
trophies.name: Break the Bank
sources: Official trophy list via Exophase and PSNProfiles
PowerPyx — GTA 6 trophy guide (no mission medals; story trophies cannot be missed)

trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Child's Play and this trophy unlocks when the mission ends. It is a straightforward story trophy: it pops automatically on completion, cannot be missed, and asks for nothing beyond finishing the mission itself. Play it when the story offers it, follow the objectives, and move on. Because GTA 6 has no mission replay and no medal system, there is no reason to replay it for a better result — one completion is all the trophy ever needs. If you are keeping manual saves per chapter, this mission will sit safely inside one of them, but you will never need to go back to it for trophy purposes.
trophies.name: Family Matters
sources: Official trophy list via Exophase and PSNProfiles
PowerPyx — GTA 6 trophy guide (story mission trophies unlock naturally)

trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Headliners and the trophy unlocks at the end of it. Another unmissable story trophy: it is awarded for finishing the mission, nothing more, and it will pop during a normal playthrough of the campaign. Headliners is one of the later named missions, so by the time you reach it you will have the full Leonida map, both protagonists and a deep bench of weapons and vehicles — use whatever loadout you are comfortable with, since the game awards no medals and the trophy does not care how stylishly you finish. Just complete the mission and the trophy is yours.
trophies.name: DWNFALL
sources: Official trophy list via Exophase and PSNProfiles
PowerPyx — GTA 6 trophy guide (story mission trophies unlock naturally)

trophies.guide: Complete the story mission VCIA Takedown and the trophy unlocks when it ends. The name gives the setting away — Vice City International Airport — so expect a mission built around aircraft, runways and a fast exit, and go in prepared for a driving or flying sequence rather than a straight shootout. Like all story mission trophies it cannot be missed: finish the mission and it pops. If you enjoy the airport as a playground, remember the separate trophy Catch Me If You Can, which asks you to make an unscheduled departure from VCIA in free roam — a different trick from this mission, and one you can try any time after the story.
trophies.name: Hi-Jacked
sources: Official trophy list via Exophase and PSNProfiles
PowerPyx — GTA 6 trophy guide (story mission trophies unlock naturally)

trophies.guide: Complete the story mission Operation Savage Glory and the trophy unlocks at its conclusion. The mission's name suggests a large, military-flavoured operation, so expect heavy combat and possibly heavy vehicles — stock up on armor and ammunition beforehand and keep a sturdy vehicle handy. As with every story mission trophy, it is unmissable: one completion is all it takes, there are no medals to chase, and no special condition beyond finishing the mission. Play it when the campaign offers it, and the trophy will pop on the mission-complete screen.
trophies.name: Snow Storm
sources: Official trophy list via Exophase and PSNProfiles
PowerPyx — GTA 6 trophy guide (story mission trophies unlock naturally)

trophies.guide: Reach 100% completion on the in-game checklist, found under Progress, then Stats, then 100% Completion, which appears after the story — though progress you made during the campaign already counts. Early guides describe the checklist as closer to 60% true completion: it asks for the story, 70 of the 80 Challenges, 42 shooting-range gold medals, 200 of 277 vehicles scanned, 100 of 255 animals studied, 250 stunts (the checklist asks for fewer than the 300 some guides mention), 15 of the 18 meditation spots, and a selection of activities and collectibles — not everything in the game. Nothing on the checklist is missable and it is all doable in free roam after the story, so treat this gold trophy as the real platinum gate: work the checklist line by line in the post-game, using this tracker's filters to see which grind trophies feed it, and it will pop when the last line turns over.
trophies.name: A Long Road
sources: Official trophy list via Exophase and PSNProfiles
PowerPyx — GTA 6 trophy guide (100% checklist contents; nothing missable)
KeenGamer — GTA 6 trophy guide (70 of 80 Challenges; 200 vehicles; 100 animals)

trophies.guide: Pull off 250 stunts across Leonida — jumps, near misses, long airtime, drifts and the other driving feats the game counts as a stunt, each one flashing up as you do it. The counter is cumulative and never resets, so the honest approach is to stunt constantly from the start: take jumps at speed whenever you see a ramp or a raised edge, thread through traffic for near misses, and use fast cars and bikes on the long straight highways around Vice City. Early guides note the 100% checklist wants 250 stunts too (some guides mention 300 for full completion), so this silver is really a milestone on the way to A Long Road rather than a separate chore. It is a long grind — expect it to be one of the last silvers to pop — but it happens mostly by itself if you drive aggressively everywhere instead of only when you remember to.
trophies.name: Cunning Stunts
sources: Official trophy list via Exophase and PSNProfiles
PowerPyx — GTA 6 trophy guide (250 stunts; 100% checklist)
KeenGamer — GTA 6 trophy guide (stunt grind)

trophies.description: Try each type of activity once.
trophies.guide: Try every type of side activity in the game at least once — early guides count nine activity types, spanning the shooting range, drone races, fishing, arcade games, bowling, meditation and the other pastimes scattered around Leonida. You do not need to master any of them or win anything; one honest attempt at each is enough, and the trophy pops when the last type registers. The simplest way to get it is to treat it as a tour: whenever you pass an activity icon on the map during the story, stop and try it, and use this tracker's kind filter to see which activity trophies are still open. Most players will earn it naturally while chasing the other activity trophies, but if it has not popped by the post-game, walk the map and try whatever you have skipped — it is one of the easiest bronzes in the list.
trophies.name: Master of None
sources: Official trophy list via Exophase and PSNProfiles
PowerPyx — GTA 6 trophy guide (nine activity types)
Our own advice from the official description

trophies.description: Earn a gold medal in all Shooting Range challenges.
trophies.guide: Earn a gold medal in every Shooting Range challenge — 42 of them across the game's two shooting ranges, by early guides' count — and this silver pops. Each challenge sets a score or accuracy bar for gold, so the practical approach is to learn one weapon class at a time, use the range's own practice runs to learn the targets' rhythm, and chase gold on the challenges you find easiest first to build confidence. Early guides call this the hardest skill trophy in the game, and it also feeds the 100% checklist, which requires all 42 golds as well. Some guides add that shooting-range golds also unlock ammo cheats, so the grind pays off twice. There is no time pressure: ranges stay open in free roam, so chip away at a few challenges between story missions rather than grinding all 42 in one sitting.
trophies.name: The Shootist
sources: Official trophy list via Exophase and PSNProfiles
PowerPyx — GTA 6 trophy guide (42 shooting-range gold medals)
KeenGamer — GTA 6 trophy guide (hardest skill trophy)

trophies.description: Win a Top Fun Drone Race at every location.
trophies.guide: Win a Top Fun drone race at all 14 locations across Leonida — early guides count 42 drone races in total, three per location, and you need at least one win at each of the 14 spots. Drone races are time trials through rings and gates, so the skill is smooth flying rather than raw speed: learn each course's line on a practice run, cut corners only where you can see the next gate, and avoid crashing, since a crash costs far more time than a cautious line. The locations unlock as you explore, so this is best done as a tour of the map in the post-game, when fast travel and a full map make hopping between locations easy. It also feeds the 100% checklist, which wants all 42 drone time trials, so expect to come back and finish the remaining races after the location wins are done.
trophies.name: Top Fun
sources: Official trophy list via Exophase and PSNProfiles
PowerPyx — GTA 6 trophy guide (14 Top Fun locations; 42 drone races)
KeenGamer — GTA 6 trophy guide (42 drone time trials for 100%)

trophies.guide: Win 20 different races — the key word is different, so repeating the same easy race twenty times will not work. Races are scattered across Leonida in several forms, including street races, off-road events and the drone races, so the trophy is really a tour of the game's racing scene: enter every race icon you pass, win it once, and move on to the next. Pick a fast, grippy car for road races and something with clearance for off-road, learn each course's corners on the first lap, and use slipstreaming on the straights. Early guides note there are far more than 20 races available, so you can skip any that frustrate you and win easier ones elsewhere. Track your wins in this tracker and the bronze pops on your twentieth distinct victory.
trophies.name: Earn Cash, Not Kudos
sources: Official trophy list via Exophase and PSNProfiles
PowerPyx — GTA 6 trophy guide (race variety)
Our own advice from the official description

trophies.description: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge.
trophies.guide: Beat Cal in a fishing challenge — a head-to-head contest where you and Cal fish the same waters and the bigger catch wins. Fishing challenges are a timing and patience game: cast where the fish are showing, watch the line tension, reel steadily rather than yanking, and do not let the fish run the line out. You will find Cal at the fishing spots around Leonida's coast and inland waters; if you lose the first challenge, you can simply try again — there is no penalty for losing and no limit on attempts. Do a little practice fishing first so you understand the reeling rhythm, then take Cal on when you are comfortable. It is one of the gentler bronzes, and a nice change of pace from the shooting and driving trophies.
trophies.name: Baited My Tackle
sources: Official trophy list via Exophase and PSNProfiles
Our own advice from the official description

trophies.guide: Finish one arcade game at any arcade in Leonida and the trophy pops. Arcades are scattered around Vice City and the wider map, and each cabinet runs a small retro game — pick whichever one looks most your speed, learn its controls from the attract screen, and play it through to the end. You do not need a high score or a perfect run, just a completed game, so this is one of the quickest bronzes on the list and a good first trophy to grab when you want a break from the story. If you get stuck on one cabinet, try another: the trophy asks for any single completed arcade game, so choose the easiest one you find and save the high-score chasing for the post-game.
trophies.name: Stick Fiddler
sources: Official trophy list via Exophase and PSNProfiles
Our own advice from the official description

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Andy.
trophies.guide: Finish Andy's mission strand through to its final mission and this trophy unlocks when that last mission ends. Andy is one of the side characters who gives you work across Leonida; his missions appear as icons on the map as the story progresses, and you work through them in order until the strand concludes. Keep an eye out for his icons between story chapters, and do not leave the strand half-finished for too long — while the trophy itself cannot be missed and the missions stay available in free roam, finishing side strands as they appear keeps the post-game cleanup short. The final mission is usually the biggest job in the strand, so go in prepared, and the bronze pops on the mission-complete screen.
trophies.name: Road to Rehabilitation
sources: Official trophy list via Exophase and PSNProfiles
PowerPyx — GTA 6 trophy guide (side strands stay available in free roam)

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Kenton.
trophies.guide: Complete Kenton's mission strand through to its final mission and the trophy pops when it ends. Kenton's jobs appear as map icons as you progress through the story; take them as they come and the strand will build toward its finale. These character strands are the game's side stories — smaller in scale than the main heists, but with their own characters, cutscenes and payoffs — and they are worth doing for the story as much as for the trophy. Nothing in the strand is missable and everything stays available in free roam after the story, so if you prefer to mainline the campaign first, you can sweep up Kenton's missions in the post-game and still earn the bronze.
trophies.name: This Was No Boat Accident
sources: Official trophy list via Exophase and PSNProfiles
PowerPyx — GTA 6 trophy guide (side strands stay available in free roam)

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Billy.
trophies.guide: Finish Billy's mission strand with its final mission and this trophy unlocks on completion. Billy's jobs show up on the map as the campaign advances; work through them in order and the strand ends with a finale that pays off the character's story. Side strands like this one are best done when they appear, since their missions often take you to corners of Leonida you would not otherwise visit — useful for exploration, vehicle scanning and animal studying on the way. The trophy cannot be missed and the missions remain available after the story, so there is no pressure, but clearing the strand early means one less thing on the post-game cleanup list.
trophies.name: The Lone Rider
sources: Official trophy list via Exophase and PSNProfiles
PowerPyx — GTA 6 trophy guide (side strands stay available in free roam)

trophies.description: Complete 8 mission strands for strangers across the state of Leonida.
trophies.guide: Complete eight full Strangers & Freaks mission strands — the oddball encounters marked across Leonida — and this silver pops. Each strand is a short chain of missions for a stranger you meet in the world, and there are more than eight available, so you can pick the ones you enjoy and skip any that frustrate you. Strands unlock as you explore and as the story advances, and their icons appear on the map, so the practical approach is to detour to every stranger icon you pass during the campaign rather than saving them all for the post-game. Some strands need both protagonists or a later chapter, so if a stranger has nothing for you yet, move on and come back later. Finish any eight strands and the silver is yours.
trophies.name: Strangers & Freaks

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Randy.
trophies.guide: Complete Randy's mission strand through to its final mission and the trophy unlocks when it ends. Randy's jobs appear on the map as the story progresses; take them in order and the strand builds to its finale. Like the other character strands, this one is unmissable and stays available in free roam after the story, so you can do it whenever it suits you — but doing side strands as they appear spreads the work out and keeps the post-game cleanup to the long grinds rather than a pile of missions. The final mission is the strand's biggest job, so arrive prepared, finish it, and the bronze pops on the mission-complete screen.
trophies.name: Supply & Demand
sources: Official trophy list via Exophase and PSNProfiles

trophies.description: Complete the final mission for Tyrone.
trophies.guide: Finish Tyrone's mission strand with its final mission and this trophy pops on completion. Tyrone's missions unlock on the map as the campaign moves forward; work through them in order and the strand concludes with its finale. Character strands are the game's way of rewarding exploration and side play, and they often pay well too, which helps with the economy trophies like Treat Yo Self and Dime on the Dollar. Nothing here is missable — the missions wait for you in free roam — so fit Tyrone's strand in whenever you are passing through his part of the map, and the bronze will come naturally.
trophies.name: Spin On This!
sources: Official trophy list via Exophase and PSNProfiles

trophies.description: Meditate at every spot across Leonida.
trophies.guide: Meditate at all 18 meditation spots across Leonida — and this is the one trophy in the whole game that early guides flag as potentially missable, so read this carefully. The first meditation is offered in Chapter 1 at Jason's house: after the mission Down to Earth, talk to Lucia in the kitchen in the morning, follow her to the balcony, and accept when she offers to show you how to meditate. That opportunity disappears once Chapter 1 ends, and it is not yet confirmed whether the trophy needs it — so do it to be safe, and keep a manual save from before it. The other spots are marked meditation locations around the map, ten locations in total by early guides' count, and the last one needs Jason and Lucia playable together, which opens after Chapter 2. Note that 100% completion only asks for 15 of the 18 spots, so this trophy is stricter than the checklist. Visit every spot, meditate, and the bronze pops on the eighteenth.
trophies.name: Positive Mental Attitude
sources: Official trophy list via Exophase and PSNProfiles
PowerPyx — GTA 6 trophy guide (Chapter 1 meditation; 18 spots; 15 for 100%)
KeenGamer — GTA 6 trophy guide (the only potentially missable trophy)

trophies.description: Hunt a unique animal for Bret.
trophies.guide: Hunt a unique animal for Bret — a special creature that only appears for this hunt, somewhere in Leonida's wilds. Bret's hunt is a tracking job: follow the clues and markers the game gives you, move quietly once you are close, and take the shot when you have a clear line, because a spooked unique animal may not give you a second chance. Use binoculars to study animals as you travel anyway, since the 100% checklist asks you to study 100 of 255 animals, and the tracking skills overlap nicely. If the hunt goes wrong, you can retry it — the trophy is for completing the hunt, not for a perfect first attempt — so take your time, watch the animal's behaviour, and finish the job for Bret.
trophies.name: Fair Game
sources: Official trophy list via Exophase and PSNProfiles
Our own advice from the official description

trophies.guide: Complete three full sets of collectible cards scattered across Leonida and this silver pops. Cards are a classic GTA collectible: small, hidden in corners, on rooftops, in alleyways and inside buildings all over the map, with each set themed around a subject. The practical approach is to sweep the map district by district rather than hunting at random — clear one area completely before moving on, and use the in-game collectible tracking if the game offers it, plus this tracker's checklist to note which sets you have finished. There are more than three sets in total, so you can complete the three easiest or most complete sets you find and leave the rest. Pair card hunting with vehicle scanning and animal studying, since you are covering the same ground anyway.
trophies.name: Don't Touch My Deck
sources: Official trophy list via Exophase and PSNProfiles
PowerPyx — GTA 6 trophy guide (collectible sets)
Our own advice from the official description

trophies.guide: Use the WAiNK app to scan 100 locations across Leonida — the in-game phone app that identifies places, vehicles and points of interest when you point it at them. The counter is cumulative, so the trick is to make scanning a habit from the very start: open the app whenever you arrive somewhere new, scan landmarks, shops, vehicles and scenery, and the count will climb steadily without ever feeling like a grind. Early guides suggest scanning vehicles and locations throughout the journey, and the 100% checklist separately wants 200 of 277 vehicles scanned, so the two goals feed each other. If you reach the post-game short of 100, take a tour of the map's towns and landmarks with the app open — every unscanned location you pass is a free point toward the trophy.
trophies.name: You WAiNKer!
sources: Official trophy list via Exophase and PSNProfiles
PowerPyx — GTA 6 trophy guide (WAiNK scanning; 200 vehicles for 100%)
KeenGamer — GTA 6 trophy guide (scan as you go)

trophies.guide: Complete 50 of the game's 80 Challenges — the eight categories of ten challenges each, covering combat, vehicles, exploration and more, tracked under Progress and then Challenges. Most challenges complete naturally as you play: driving feats, combat milestones, exploration goals and activity firsts all count, so a normal campaign will quietly tick off a large number before you ever look at the list. Open the Challenges menu early, note which ones are nearly done, and let the near-complete ones steer your play for a while — finishing the easy ones first gets you to 50 fast. Remember the 100% checklist wants 70 of the 80, so this bronze is really the halfway mark on a longer grind: keep the list open during the post-game and work through the remaining categories one at a time.
trophies.name: One Last Thing
sources: Official trophy list via Exophase and PSNProfiles
PowerPyx — GTA 6 trophy guide (80 Challenges in 8 categories; 70 for 100%)
KeenGamer — GTA 6 trophy guide (Challenges under Progress)

trophies.description: Lose a 4 star Wanted Level with your partner and escape the heat.
trophies.guide: Build up a four-star wanted level while your partner is with you, then lose the cops and escape — the classic GTA heat-dodging trophy, with a duo twist. The recipe is simple: get your partner in the car, commit enough crimes to raise the wanted level to four stars, then break line of sight and hide until the stars blink and fade. Use the map to your advantage: dive into the countryside, use tunnels, alleyways and water to break pursuit, and switch vehicles if the cops have your plate. Four stars means helicopters and roadblocks, so do not try to outrun them in a straight line — break contact, stay out of the search cones, and wait it out somewhere quiet. It pops the moment the wanted level clears with your partner still beside you.
trophies.name: Hot Together
sources: Official trophy list via Exophase and PSNProfiles
Our own advice from the official description

trophies.description: Rob 3 shops back-to-back with your partner without losing your Wanted Level.
trophies.guide: Rob three shops in a row with your partner at your side, without ever losing your wanted level between robberies — the wanted level must stay active from the first till to the third. Plan a route first: pick three shops close together in Vice City, ideally on the same street or block, and scout them so you know the entrances and the getaway. Hit the first, grab the cash, get back in the car with your partner, and drive straight to the next — speed matters more than stealth here, because the trick is keeping the heat, not losing it. Keep the car healthy, avoid crashing into police, and do not stop to fight: the trophy pops when the third till is emptied and you are still wanted. If the wanted level drops, start the chain again.
trophies.name: Retail Therapy
sources: Official trophy list via Exophase and PSNProfiles
Our own advice from the official description

trophies.guide: Discover 100 different vehicles across Leonida — cars, bikes, boats, planes and everything else with an engine, each one counting the first time you find or drive it. The counter grows naturally as you play, since the story alone puts you in dozens of different vehicles, but the fastest route to 100 is deliberate variety: steal or borrow anything you have not driven yet, scan unfamiliar vehicles with the WAiNK app as you go, and visit car parks, docks, airfields and dealerships where new models cluster. Early guides note the 100% checklist wants 200 of 277 vehicles scanned, so this bronze is the halfway point of a much bigger collection — and the game tracks a total of 277 base models, so there is plenty of room to find your hundred. Check this tracker's progress and take a tour of the map's garages and showrooms if you stall.
trophies.name: Whip It Good
sources: Official trophy list via Exophase and PSNProfiles
PowerPyx — GTA 6 trophy guide (200 of 277 vehicles for 100%)
KeenGamer — GTA 6 trophy guide (scan vehicles as you go)

trophies.description: Take down 5 enemies in a single use of Combat Focus.
trophies.guide: Take down five enemies during one single use of Combat Focus — the game's slow-motion aiming mode — and the trophy pops. Combat Focus gives you a short window of slowed time, so the trick is to set the scene before you trigger it: find a spot where five or more enemies are grouped together, ideally in an open area with clear lines of fire, and make sure your weapon is loaded and your health is full. Trigger Combat Focus, work through the targets methodically with headshots or quick body shots, and do not waste the window on reloading. A mission or a gang hideout with clustered enemies is the natural place to try it, and if you fall short, just retry — there is no penalty, and you can attempt it as many times as you like in free roam once you know a good spot.
trophies.name: Gunslinger
sources: Official trophy list via Exophase and PSNProfiles
Our own advice from the official description

trophies.description: Make an unscheduled departure at VCIA.
trophies.guide: Make an unscheduled departure from Vice City International Airport — in plain terms, steal a plane and take off without a flight plan, or leave the airport in a way the tower did not schedule. The natural approach is to get airside at VCIA, find a parked plane on the tarmac or in a hangar, get in, and take off down a runway while the airport's security reacts — expect a wanted level, so be ready to climb fast and head for open sky. Alternatively, a helicopter grabbed from the airport apron and flown straight out counts as an unscheduled departure too. Do it in free roam when you are not mid-mission, keep the aircraft steady on takeoff, and the trophy pops once you are airborne and clear of the airport. It is a quick, fun bronze and a good excuse to explore VCIA.
trophies.name: Catch Me If You Can
sources: Official trophy list via Exophase and PSNProfiles
Our own advice from the official description

trophies.guide: Get involved with Rhino tanks — the military armour that shows up when the heat gets serious — and this trophy pops for the encounter. The description is deliberately vague, as befits a hidden-style trophy, but the shape of it is clear: reach a high wanted level, ideally five stars, until the military rolls in with Rhinos, then deal with them — steal one, destroy one, or simply survive the encounter. The practical route is to cause chaos in an open area with room to manoeuvre, let the wanted level climb to the top, and watch for the tanks. Going in on foot is a quick way to get flattened, so have a fast vehicle ready, use explosives or heavy weapons if you have them, and remember that stealing a Rhino is both the most fun and the most useful outcome. One good tank encounter is all it takes.
trophies.name: Challenging Tank
sources: Official trophy list via Exophase and PSNProfiles
Our own advice from the official description

trophies.description: Rob a jewelry store without being detected.
trophies.guide: Rob a jewelry store cleanly, without ever being detected — a stealth job, not a smash-and-grab. Plan it like a heist: scout the store first, learn the guard patrols and camera positions, and go in quiet — suppressed weapons if you have them, no alarms, no witnesses raising the alarm, and no police called. Move through the store, empty the displays, and get out before anyone realises what happened; if you are spotted, the attempt fails, so leave immediately and try again rather than fighting your way out. Night-time attempts and a quiet approach help, and doing it with a plan beats doing it loudly. One clean, undetected robbery is all the trophy needs, and it pairs well with the other robbery trophies once you know the store layouts.
trophies.name: Sneakthief

trophies.guide: Rob five bank vaults and escape cleanly after each one — a silver that turns bank robbery into a repeatable profession. Bank vaults are the big scores: each one needs planning, a way in, and a getaway, and you must escape the wanted level after the robbery for it to count. Space the jobs out, scout each bank's surroundings for escape routes, and keep a fast car or bike stashed nearby before you go in. Five vaults is a commitment, so treat it as a post-game project: one vault per session, careful escapes, and the silver pops on the fifth successful getaway. The money helps too — it feeds the economy trophies — and by the time you have done five, you will know Leonida's banks and backstreets better than anyone.
trophies.name: Maximum Withdrawal

trophies.description: Rob an Armored Truck and escape.
trophies.guide: Rob an armored truck and escape with the loot. Armored trucks drive set routes around Leonida, usually with an escort or a guard, so the job is to intercept one — ram it to a stop or block its route, break it open, grab the cash, and then lose the wanted level that follows. Pick a quiet stretch of road where you control the escape, rather than a busy downtown junction where the police arrive in seconds. A heavy vehicle for the ram and a fast one stashed nearby for the getaway is the classic combination, and explosives will open a stubborn truck faster than gunfire. Once the cash is in hand, break line of sight, switch vehicles if you can, and wait out the heat — the trophy pops when you escape clean.
trophies.name: A Classic Blitz Play
sources: Official trophy list via Exophase and PSNProfiles

trophies.guide: Explore every area of Leonida — all 52 areas, by early guides' count — from Vice City's neon streets to the swamps, beaches and small towns of the wider state. The game tracks which areas you have visited, so the trophy is a sightseeing tour: drive the highways, take the back roads, visit every town, beach, island and landmark, and the map will fill in as you go. The fastest way is a deliberate road trip in the post-game, when the whole map is open and fast travel lets you hop between regions, but you will cover most of it naturally during the story and side missions. Use this tracker's exploration filter to see what is left, pair the tour with vehicle scanning and animal studying, and the bronze pops when the last area registers.
trophies.name: The Goodtime State

trophies.description: Rob an Illegal Operation belonging to each gang.
trophies.guide: Rob one illegal operation belonging to each of the nine gangs in Leonida — a tour of the state's criminal underworld, one gang at a time. Illegal operations are the gangs' money-making sites: stash houses, labs, chop shops and the like, marked for robbery once you find them. Each gang controls its own turf, so the trophy takes you all over the map — learn which gang holds which neighbourhood, hit one operation per gang, and get out clean. Go in prepared, since these sites are guarded, and scout the escape route before you start shooting. The count is per gang, not per operation, so nine careful robberies is the whole job; early guides count nine gangs, and this tracker lets you tick them off one by one as you work through the list.
trophies.name: Pest Control

trophies.description: Enjoy a cocktail with a view on Ocean Beach.
trophies.guide: Head to Ocean Beach, order a cocktail, and enjoy it with the view — one of the game's pure flavour trophies, and a reminder to slow down. Ocean Beach is Vice City's famous beachfront strip, so walk the promenade, find a beach bar or a spot with a sea view, and order the cocktail through the interaction prompt. There is no timer, no challenge and no enemy to fight: just sit, sip, and watch the ocean while the trophy pops. It is best done at sunset, when the beach looks its best, and it pairs beautifully with the exploration trophy — you will be visiting the beach anyway while you work through Leonida's 52 areas, so stop for a drink while you are there.
trophies.name: In The Beginning…

trophies.description: Smash your way out of a vehicle showroom in classic style.
trophies.guide: Drive a vehicle straight through a showroom's glass front and out the other side, in the classic GTA style — the kind of stunt the series has celebrated since its earliest games. Find a vehicle showroom with a big glass facade, pick a fast car, line up a run at the windows, and floor it: the trophy pops when you smash out through the glass and keep going. The showroom's owners and the police will not be thrilled, so expect a wanted level and plan your escape route before you hit the glass. It is a one-and-done bronze — a single glorious smash is all it takes — so choose your moment, aim straight, and enjoy the most cinematic trophy on the list.
trophies.name: Capital Offense

trophies.description: Follow-through at the Kolt & Associates' bowling alley.
trophies.guide: Go bowling at the Kolt & Associates bowling alley and follow through — in other words, play a full game of bowling there, from the first frame to the last. Bowling is one of the game's side activities, with its own aiming and power mechanics: line up the shot, set the power, and release smoothly, aiming for the pocket between the head pin and its neighbour. You do not need a perfect game or even a win — just complete a game at this specific alley, following through on every frame. The alley is easy to find once you know the name, and the trophy pops when the game ends. It is a relaxed bronze, best enjoyed with a partner or between bigger jobs.

trophies.guide: This is one of the game's hidden trophies, and its vague description is deliberately unhelpful — PlayStation hides it until you earn it. The name and wording point at Jason and Lucia's partnership reaching a wide audience: a moment where the duo's exploits get noticed, shared or celebrated across Leonida. Early guides have not yet pinned down the exact trigger, so the honest advice is to keep playing the duo's story and side content together, use the WAiNK app and the in-game social features when they appear, and let the partnership moments come to you. Do not chase this one specifically in the early game; it is likely to pop naturally during the campaign or the post-game cleanup. We will update this guide when the community confirms the trigger — check the sources below for the latest reports.

trophies.guide: Make choices across the campaign — the decisions that shape Jason and Lucia's story — and this trophy tracks them. PlayStation tracks a count for it, reportedly up to 500 choices, which suggests it is less about one big decision and more about the accumulation of small ones: dialogue choices, approach choices in missions, and the way you handle the duo's relationship across the chapters. Because there is no mission replay, early guides strongly recommend keeping manual saves before major story crossroads, so a choice you regret can be revisited without replaying the whole game. Play naturally, make the choices that feel right, keep your save rotation healthy, and the trophy will pop as the count builds. It is a campaign-long tracker, not a single moment.

trophies.guide: Succeed on a second attempt at something you first failed — the game's gentle nod to persistence. The exact trigger is one of the hidden trophies' small mysteries: it may be tied to a specific retry, such as failing and then passing a particular challenge, mission beat or activity on the second go. The practical approach is not to force it but to keep playing: fail a race or a challenge, try again immediately, and succeed — most players will earn it without ever thinking about it, because everyone fails something on the first try. If it has not popped by the post-game, retry any activity you once failed and finish it on the second attempt. It is a bronze that rewards not giving up, and it costs nothing to earn.

trophies.guide: Witness something strange in Leonida — the game's nod to the weird, random events that have always hidden in GTA's worlds. The description is deliberately cryptic, and early guides have not confirmed the exact trigger, but the shape of it is familiar to series veterans: a random encounter, an unexplained sighting, or a strange event out in the world that you happen to be present for. The best approach is to explore widely and keep your eyes open — drive the back roads, visit the swamps and the remote corners of the map at different times of day, and investigate anything unusual rather than driving past it. It will likely pop when you least expect it, which is exactly the point. Check the sources below for community reports as players pin the trigger down.

trophies.description: Bowl 'em over with a melee drive-by.
trophies.guide: Knock someone down with a melee drive-by — that is, strike a pedestrian or an enemy with a melee weapon while driving past in a vehicle. The technique is pure GTA: get a car or a bike, pick up a melee weapon such as a bat, cruise slowly past a target on the sidewalk, and swing as you pass. Bikes work best, since you can lean into the swing and keep your speed, but a car with an open window does the job too. Pick a quiet street so you can line the pass up without traffic in the way, and do not worry about the wanted level — a single hit is quick, and the trophy pops the moment the target goes down. One clean melee drive-by is all it takes.

trophies.description: Earn $250,000 laundering Marked Bills through your contacts.
trophies.guide: Launder $250,000 of Marked Bills through your contacts and this bronze pops. Marked Bills are the dirty cash you pick up from robberies and heists, and they cannot be spent directly — you move them through contacts who clean the money for a cut. The practical route is to keep robbing: bank vaults, armored trucks, shops and illegal operations all pay in marked bills, so the laundering total climbs alongside the heist trophies. Find your contacts, hand the bills over in batches, and watch the laundered total grow in the stats screen. It is a cumulative $250,000, not a single transaction, so there is no need to hoard bills for one big wash — launder as you earn, and the trophy will pop during the post-game cleanup, especially if you are also working on Maximum Withdrawal.

trophies.guide: Spend $100,000 across all the shops in Leonida — clothes, weapons, ammunition, food, vehicle mods, whatever you like — and the bronze pops once your lifetime spending crosses the line. The total is cumulative across every shop, so you do not need to blow it all in one place or in one trip. In practice, the big-ticket items do the heavy lifting: weapon upgrades, vehicle modifications and property purchases all count, so a normal playthrough with a few upgrades will get you most of the way there. If you reach the post-game short of the target, buy the most expensive thing you can find — a top-end vehicle mod or a premium weapon — and the last few thousand will vanish quickly. Check the stats screen to see how much you have spent so far.
trophies.name: Treat Yo Self
sources: Official trophy list via Exophase and PSNProfiles

trophies.guide: Buy every garage property in the game — eight of them, by early guides' count — and this bronze pops when the last deed is signed. Garages are the properties that let you store and customise your vehicle collection, and they are scattered across Leonida's towns and neighbourhoods, each with its own price. You will need a healthy bank balance, so do this in the post-game once the heists and laundering have filled your wallet — the money from Maximum Withdrawal and Dime on the Dollar goes a long way here. Visit each property's for-sale sign, buy it, and move on to the next; the trophy pops on the eighth purchase. Owning the full set also makes the vehicle-collection trophies far easier, since you finally have somewhere to keep everything you discover.

trophies.description: Register 10 vehicles to the Scooter Bros app.
trophies.guide: Register ten vehicles to the Scooter Bros app — the in-game service for managing and calling your rides. Open the app on your phone, follow its prompts to register a vehicle you own or have just acquired, and repeat until ten are on the books. The app is the game's way of keeping your fleet organised, so the natural route is to register the vehicles you actually drive: your favourite cars and bikes first, then anything interesting you pick up while exploring. Each registration is quick, and the count is cumulative, so you can do them one at a time as you find new vehicles or all at once in the post-game when your garage is full. Ten registrations and the bronze pops — and it pairs neatly with Whip It Good, since discovering vehicles and registering them go hand in hand.
